translations.\"Yes\" means an administrator enforced: "Yes" means an administrator enforced this rule: nobody else can edit or disable it, and since enforced rules fill the first four bands, no personal rule can come before it.
translations.A disabled rule cannot be applied — enab: A disabled rule cannot be applied — enable it first.
translations.A granted app password may read across a: A granted app password may read across accounts through the /api/v1/sudo/ routes without anyone typing a password. A grant stays in force until it is revoked, and every administrator can see it. Create the app password under "Security" first, with "Allow filesystem access" on. Whether you may look across accounts at all is still up to your administrator; a grant replaces the password prompt, not the permission.

Administrator-enforced rules covering every storage there is.
translations.Administrator-enforced rules for one acc: Administrator-enforced rules for one account's home folder or one storage. No other rule comes before them there, and the account cannot edit or disable them.
translations.Administrator-enforced rules for the mem: Administrator-enforced rules for the members of a group, or for one team folder. Only an enforced rule aimed at something more specific comes before them.

Who may look across accounts at all is decided under "Who may look across accounts"; a grant replaces the password prompt, not the permission.

translations.Creating and editing rules for folders i: Creating and editing rules for folders in one's own files that one can write to. An administrator always may; a rule an administrator has enforced is read-only for everyone else regardless.
translations.Defaults for all home folders. Within th: Defaults for all home folders. Within this band a catch-all default — path "**", "/" or empty — always evaluates last, after the more specific rules here.
translations.Drag to reorder among the rules of the s: Drag to reorder among the rules of the same scope
translations.Evaluated top to bottom — the first matc: Evaluated top to bottom — the first matching rule decides the file. A rule's band follows from its scope and whether it is enforced, so enforced rules always precede personal rules, and the catch-all default is last. Drag a rule by its handle to reorder it among the rules of the same scope; to move it to another band, change its scope or its "Enforced" setting.
translations.Every rule that can affect your files, i: Every rule that can affect your files, in the order they are evaluated — the first match decides. Rules an administrator enforced come first and are read-only; your own rules come next and are yours to edit and reorder; the defaults below them apply only where none of your rules matched. You can create rules only if you have been given permission and the path is a folder in your own files that you can write to.
translations.Find other files sharing a checksum with: Find other files sharing a checksum with this file.
translations.Glob pattern the file path must match. \: Glob pattern the file path must match. "**" matches every file, "**/*.txt" matches by extension, and "/Documents/**" matches everything below one folder.
Glob pattern the file path must match. "**" matches every file; "/Documents/**" matches everything below that folder. Rules are checked in order and the first match wins.

translations.Individual accounts that may call the pu: Individual accounts that may call the public API with an app password, in addition to the members of any selected groups.
translations.Individual accounts that may create and: Individual accounts that may create and edit rules for folders in their own files that they can write to, in addition to the members of any selected groups.
translations.Individual accounts that may look at oth: Individual accounts that may look at other accounts' files once they have confirmed their password, in addition to the members of any selected groups and of the admin group.
translations.Individual accounts that may recalculate: Individual accounts that may recalculate checksums by hand, in addition to the members of any selected groups.

translations.Members of these groups may create and e: Members of these groups may create and edit rules for folders in their own files that they can write to. Selected groups and selected accounts are combined — being in either is enough.
translations.Members of these groups may look across: Members of these groups may look across accounts once they have confirmed their password. Selected groups and selected accounts are combined — being in either is enough.
translations.Members of these groups may recalculate: Members of these groups may recalculate checksums by hand. Selected groups and selected accounts are combined — being in either is enough.

translations.Recalculating checksums by hand: the sid: Recalculating checksums by hand: the sidebar's "Recalculate" buttons, "Verify" and "Verify all" on the Duplicates page, and the API's recalculation routes, for any file the account can reach. Reading checksums already computed is not affected. Without this permission neither the sidebar nor the Duplicates page shows the buttons, and the API refuses the request.
translations.Rules are evaluated in band order and th: Rules are evaluated in band order and the first match decides the file. A rule's band follows from its scope and whether it is enforced — it is not chosen directly, and reordering only moves a rule among the rules of the same scope.
translations.Rules for a group's members, or for one: Rules for a group's members, or for one team folder. Not enforced: for a member's home folder, their personal rule comes first.
translations.Rules for one account's home folder — pe: Rules for one account's home folder — personal rules — or for one storage. They decide a file only where no enforced rule matched it first.
translations.Scripts and other apps calling this app': Scripts and other apps calling this app's public API with an app password. The bundled pages — this one, the Duplicates page, the file sidebar — keep working for everyone; this decides who may reach the same routes from outside them.

translations.Show only groups whose hash matches what: Show only groups whose hash matches what you type. Whole values come first, then those that start with what you typed. Turn on "Match anywhere in the hash" to match it in the middle of a hash too. Upper case is fine.
translations.Smallest group to list: files sharing a: Smallest group to list: files sharing a checksum, 2 to 100
translations.That view needs your password confirmed: That view needs your password confirmed again, or is not yours to look at.
translations.The \"All home folders\" default covers: The "All home folders" default covers home folders only: files on external storage and in team folders are reached only by the "Everything" default or by their own team-folder or storage rules.
translations.The algorithm the Checksums tab in the f: The algorithm the Checksums tab in the file sidebar offers as its first button. Leave it on the default to follow the server; pick one to have it first for every file, with the file's own rule providing the second button.
translations.The algorithm used wherever none is name: The algorithm used wherever none is named: new rules, the command line, the API, and the sidebar's first button for anyone who has not chosen one. Only an allowed algorithm can be the default; removing the default from the list above makes the first remaining one the default.
translations.The algorithms rules may compute and pic: The algorithms rules may compute and pickers may offer, chosen from what this server's PHP provides. Removing one does not delete checksums already stored under it — they stay searchable — it only stops new ones being computed.
translations.The default must be one of the allowed a: The default must be one of the allowed algorithms.

translations.The last resort, covering every storage: The last resort, covering every storage — external storage and team folders included. Enable deliberately: it can reach storage that is slow or costs money to read.

translations.The path leads into a received share, a: The path leads into a received share, a team folder or another mounted storage. A personal rule only governs your own files; those files are governed by their owner's or the folder's own rules.
translations.The raw ID from the storages table, matc: The raw ID from the storages table, matched exactly, whatever kind of storage it names. Use this for external storage, or for any storage the other choices cannot address.

translations.The sudoers: members of the admin group: The sudoers: members of the admin group always, plus the groups and accounts selected here. A group admin may also look at the members of the groups they administer without being selected. Looking across accounts still needs a password confirmation, which holds for 30 minutes, or a granted app password; this only says who may be asked.
translations.The team folder this rule addresses. Eve: The team folder this rule addresses. Every member sees the same files, and the rule follows the folder — not whoever happens to look at it.
translations.The team folder this rule names, or the: The team folder this rule names, or the app that provides it, is not available, so the rule can never match.
translations.These places exist on this server but ha: These places exist on this server but have no catch-all rule of their own, so their files are decided by a more general rule, or by none at all. "Add rule" opens the dialogue with a catch-all rule for the place; it is only stored once you click "Save" there.

translations.This tab shows other people's files: tho: This tab shows other people's files: those of the accounts and groups chosen above. Leave this tab to go back to your own.
translations.Up to this many, the picker opens with e: Up to this many, the picker opens with every account and group it may offer already in the list. Above it, the picker asks the server as you type instead. Applies to administrators and group admins alike.

translations.What happens to a file that already has: What happens to a file that already has checksums. "Auto" recalculates only outdated ones, "Missing" also adds missing ones, "Force" deletes and recalculates all of them, and "Lazy" deletes them now and lets a later run recalculate them.

What happens to a file that already has checksums. "auto" recalculates only outdated ones, "missing" also adds missing ones, "force" deletes and recalculates all of them, and "lazy" deletes them now and lets a later run recalculate them. Shown as "—" for a rule that computes nothing.
translations.What happens when this rule matches. \"I: What happens when this rule matches. "Include" computes the checksums below. "Ignore" stops automatic hashing but still lets someone recalculate a file's checksums by hand. "Exclude" blocks hashing entirely — use it for storage that must not be read, such as a metered external mount.
translations.What happens when this rule matches. \"i: What happens when this rule matches. "include" computes the checksums in this row. "ignore" stops automatic hashing but still allows a manual recalculation. "exclude" blocks hashing by every route, including the sidebar button, the API and the occ command.
translations.When on, every account may call the publ: When on, every account may call the public API with an app password. When off, only the groups and individual accounts selected here may; the app's own pages keep working for everyone.
translations.When on, every account may create and ed: When on, every account may create and edit rules for folders in their own files that they can write to. When off, only the groups and individual accounts you select may.
translations.When on, every account may look across a: When on, every account may look across all accounts after confirming their password. When off, only members of the admin group and the groups and accounts selected here may.
translations.When on, every account may recalculate c: When on, every account may recalculate checksums by hand. When off, only the groups and individual accounts selected here may; everyone still sees the checksums already computed.
translations.When set, nobody else can edit or disabl: When set, nobody else can edit or disable this rule. Enforced rules are evaluated before every personal rule, so none can come before them.
translations.Where the rule sits in evaluation order:: Where the rule sits in evaluation order: its band, and its position among the rules of the same scope in that band, joined by a dot, so 7.1 is the first rule of band 7. The first rule that matches a file decides it outright, so a lower number is stronger. The band follows from the rule's scope and whether it is enforced — it is never chosen directly — and the position is what dragging changes.
translations.Whether the rule takes part in evaluatio: Whether the rule takes part in evaluation at all. A disabled rule is skipped as though it were not there, so the next matching rule decides instead.
translations.Which algorithms this server computes, f: Which algorithms this server computes, from what its PHP provides, and which of them is the default. Rules may only use these, and every picker in the app offers exactly these.
translations.Which files get checksums, with which al: Which files get checksums, with which algorithms, and which are left alone. Rules act when a file is created or changed, and a background job applies them to existing files after a few minutes.
translations.Which files the rule addresses: one acco: Which files the rule addresses: one account's home folder, the home folders of one group's members, "All home folders", one team folder, one storage by its ID, or "Everything". A rule only ever meets files inside its scope — "All home folders" reaches every home folder and nothing else, while "Everything" also reaches team folders and external storage.
translations.Which files this rule addresses: all hom: Which files this rule addresses: all home folders, the home folders of one group's members, a single account's home folder, one team folder, one storage by its raw ID, or everything — every storage, external storage and team folders included.
